summary: Coos FPA lookout on Kenyon Mountain, OR: tree station, 1935 CCC tower, 1961 tower replaced by a camera; tower removed about 2011; present site not described.

facts.design: Last tower: 53-ft treated wood with flat-roof live-in cab (ODF cab); earlier 100-ft timber tower with L-6 cab (1935)
facts.status_note: Tower removed about 2011 (May 26, 2011 per Oregon Lookouts timeline). NHLR entry from 2003 still says in active service.

events.note: Lookout at Kenyon mountain reported a new fire (Morning Register, quoted on Oregon Lookouts page); earliest staffed reference in sources read
Coos Bay Times lists Signal Tree as a new station near Camas Valley; NHLR dates the first cupola cabin only to the 1920s
Glade A. Sanford took the lookout post at Signal Tree, replacing J.F. Burkhart, whose school had started on September 2nd (Coos Bay Times, September 6, 1930)
Substitute to be provided after Carl Beeson was unable to take charge of the station through sickness
CCC crew from Camp Bradford completed a 100-ft tower to replace the old tree and platform; NHLR gives 100-ft timber tower with L-6 cab, Oregon Lookouts timeline gives 110 ft
Coos District annual report: 1935 tower demolished and replaced by a 50-ft CT-3 treated timber tower
The World, May 20, 1960 (quoted on Oregon Lookouts page): 50-ft tower being erected to replace the 110-ft tower; conflicts with the 1959 and 1961 dates
Present 53-ft treated wood tower with Oregon Department of Forestry flat-roof live-in cab (NHLR; firelookout.com says built 1961)
Coos District annual report: Elk Mountain serves as a replacement for Brewster Rock, Signal Tree and Blue Ridge lookouts
6 x 8 ft cement block building for radio-repeater equipment completed at the Signal Tree lookout site
Tower removed May 26, 2011 (Oregon Lookouts timeline); firelookout.com says it came down about 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1959 annual report says demolished and replaced; a May 1960 newspaper says being erected; NHLR and firelookout.com say built 1961. The story gives the range and does not pick one.
53 ft per NHLR and firelookout.com; 50 ft per the 1959 annual report and the 1960 newspaper.
100 ft per NHLR, firelookout.com and the CCC account; 110 ft per the Oregon Lookouts timeline and the 1960 newspaper.
NHLR says a cupola cabin from the 1920s; the Oregon Lookouts page describes a red fir with a pipe ladder. The story reports both.
NHLR (registered 2003) says in active service; firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts timeline say a camera replaced the tower and the tower came down about 2011.

corrections.why: 30.5 m (100 ft) is the 1935 tower. The last tower standing is listed at 53 ft (16.2 m) by NHLR and firelookout.com; the 1960 newspaper gives 50 ft.

notes_for_editor: Present site not described by any source read. Search results (not read, so not cited) include a sixes.net KSOR page on Kenyon Mountain with 2008 photos and an amateur-radio repeater listing for Kenyon Mt. (redcrosscommunications.org); either may describe what stands on the summit now and should be read before any site-today claim is added. A cherylhill.net post says the tower was torn down in May, which fits the 2011 date. NHLR's 'in active service' text is stale. The 1935 and 1961 dates and the 100/110 ft and 50/53 ft figures conflict across sources and the story presents them as conflicting. Access level not established; no access fact recorded.
